questions.stem: A 2 kW heater is used for 3 hours. How many kilowatt-hours (kWh) of energy does it use?
questions.explanation: Energy in kWh = power (kW) x time (hours) = 2 x 3 = 6 kWh. Option A (1.5) divides power by time. Option C (6000) converts to watts incorrectly. Option D divides time by power. When using kWh, keep power in kW and time in hours — do not convert to watts and seconds.

questions.stem: Electricity costs 30p per kWh. A 100 W lamp is left on for 10 hours. What is the cost?
questions.explanation: First convert power: 100 W = 0.1 kW. Energy = 0.1 kW x 10 h = 1 kWh. Cost = 1 kWh x 30p = 30p. Option B (300p) forgets to convert watts to kilowatts (uses 100 instead of 0.1). Option C (3p) incorrectly calculates 0.1 x 30/10. Always convert watts to kilowatts by dividing by 1000 before calculating kWh.

questions.stem: A 500 W microwave is used for 5 minutes. How much energy is transferred in joules?
questions.explanation: When working in joules, use E = P x t with power in watts and time in seconds. Time = 5 minutes = 5 x 60 = 300 s. E = 500 x 300 = 150,000 J (150 kJ). Option A (2,500) uses minutes instead of seconds (500 x 5). Always convert time to seconds when calculating energy in joules.

questions.stem: A household uses 3200 kWh of electricity per year. Electricity costs 28p per kWh. What is the annual electricity cost?
questions.explanation: Cost = energy x price per unit = 3200 x 28p = 89,600p. Converting to pounds: 89,600 / 100 = £896.00. Option A (£89.60) is off by a factor of 10. Option C (£8,960) is off by a factor of 10 in the other direction. Option D divides energy by price. Be careful with the pence-to-pounds conversion.

questions.stem: A student wants to reduce their household electricity bill. Which change would save the most energy?

options.text: Replacing a 10 W LED lamp used for 5 hours a day with a 5 W LED
Replacing a 2000 W tumble dryer used for 1 hour a day with a washing line
Switching off a 50 W TV on standby (5 W) when not watching
Using a more efficient phone charger (5 W instead of 10 W)

questions.explanation: The tumble dryer uses 2000 W x 1 h = 2 kWh per day. Eliminating this saves 2 kWh daily. The LED change saves (10-5) x 5 = 25 Wh = 0.025 kWh per day. Switching off TV standby saves about 5 W x 19 h = 95 Wh = 0.095 kWh. The phone charger saves 5 W x a few hours = negligible. The tumble dryer saves by far the most because it has the highest power rating. High-power appliances offer the biggest savings.
